topic: Git Directed Acyclic Graph and Content-Addressed Object Model

claims.statement: Logically, Git represents version history as a Directed Acyclic Graph of complete filesystem snapshots rather than change-delta sequences.
claims.verifiableSource: Chacon S, Straub B. (Pro Git, 2nd Edition, Apress 2014)
claims.evidenceLocation: Chapter 10: Git Internals - Git Objects & Plumbing
claims.truthCondition: Each commit object contains a pointer to a root tree object capturing the complete project directory structure at that point in time
claims.simplificationBoundaries: While logically snapshots, Git physically uses packfiles with directed delta compression (git pack-objects) on disk to minimize network and disk overhead
claims.predictiveQuestion: How does Git logically store repository history?
claims.predictedAnswer: As an immutable Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of project snapshots, not file diffs

claims.statement: Git Blob objects store only raw file contents compressed with zlib; filenames, timestamps, and permissions are stored separately in Tree objects.
claims.verifiableSource: Torvalds L. (Git Source Code, cache.h & object-file.c)
claims.truthCondition: Blob SHA-1 is computed as sha1('blob ' + size + '\0' + content); identical files share the exact same Blob regardless of filename or path
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Git originally used SHA-1 (160-bit); transitioning to SHA-256 (256-bit) via objectFormat configuration
claims.predictiveQuestion: Where is a file's name stored in Git's object database?
claims.predictedAnswer: In the parent Tree object that references the Blob, never inside the Blob object itself

claims.statement: A Git branch is a lightweight 41-byte movable reference containing only the 40-character hex SHA of its latest commit tip.
claims.verifiableSource: Pro Git Book, Section 3.1: Git Branches in a Nutshell
claims.truthCondition: Branch creation does not copy project files; it creates a plain text file containing a 40-character commit hash plus a newline
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Packed references in .git/packed-refs aggregate multiple branch heads into a single sorted index for lookup performance
claims.predictiveQuestion: Why are Git branch creation and switching nearly instantaneous?
claims.predictedAnswer: A branch is merely a 41-byte pointer to a commit hash in the immutable DAG, requiring zero file replication
